questions.hint: Use circle theorems: angle at centre, angle in a semicircle, isosceles triangles from radii.
questions.solution:
Since \(JL\) and \(KM\) are perpendicular diameters, \(\triangle JOK\) is a right isosceles triangle (\(OJ = OK\)).
\(\alpha = \angle OJK = (180^\circ - 90^\circ) / 2 = 45^\circ\).
Similarly, \(\beta = \angle OKL = 45^\circ\).

steps.explain: Find $\alpha$ using the properties of a cyclic quadrilateral.
steps.work:
The points \(P, Q, R, S\) lie on the circle, forming a cyclic quadrilateral. Opposite interior angles sum to \(180^\circ\).

\(\alpha + \angle PQR = 180^\circ\)

\(\alpha + 95^\circ = 180^\circ\)

\(\alpha = 180^\circ - 95^\circ\)

\(\alpha = 85^\circ\)

steps.explain: Use the isosceles triangle $\Delta OQR$ to find $\angle OQR$.
steps.work:
\(\Delta OQR\) is isosceles because \(OQ\) and \(OR\) are radii. The base angles are equal.

\(\angle OQR = \angle QRO\)

\(\angle OQR = 35^\circ\)

steps.explain: Find $\beta$ using the isosceles triangle $\Delta OPQ$.
steps.work:
The total angle \(\angle PQR = 95^\circ\). We know \(\angle OQR = 35^\circ\).

\(\angle PQO = 95^\circ - 35^\circ = 60^\circ\)

\(\Delta OPQ\) is isosceles (\(OP = OQ\)), so the base angles are equal.

\(\beta = \angle PQO\)

\(\beta = 60^\circ\)
